To stay in orbit you need to be in space or the drag from the atmosphere \nwill slow you down. If you were to try orbiting in the atmosphere, you would \nneed to have the engines running all the time - which isn't really orbiting.

Around Kerbin there is a thin layer of atmosphere. This layer is densest near \nthe ground and thins out to nothing as you get to space. Kerbin isn't the only \nplanet like this, but for this section it is what's important.
Around Kerbin the atmosphere extends 70km from sea level, to where space \nbegins.
Getting back down is relatively simple. You burn in the \nretrograde direction which will slow the vessel \nenough to return to the surface.
You only need to slow the vessel enough to \nget inside the atmosphere, aerodynamic \ndrag will slow you a lot as well.
